newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Mortars fired on Moslem-held quarter of Mostar.
newsitem.headline: Mortars fired on Moslem-held quarter of Mostar.

text.p: Two mortar bombs were fired on Moslem-held eastern Mostar early on Saturday morning in a serious violation of the Dayton peace agreement, an international police monitor reported.

"Two 60mm rounds were fired," Frank Sarver of the International Police Task Force told Reuters. "One struck a residence on the east side of Mostar, causing damage to a residence." The second mortar bomb did not explode, he said.

The attack occurred after 1 a.m. not far from the Carinski bridge in the town centre, Sarver said by telephone. There were no injuries reported. Bosnian Moslem media in east Mostar said the mortar bomb hit a building housing two families.
The NATO-led peace force said it was investigating the incident but could not confirm where the mortar bomb impacted in the town, which is strictly divided into Moslem and Croat sectors.
The report comes after the worst violence in troubled Mostar city since a peace agreeement was signed in 1995 erupted in the city last Monday.
One man died when armed Croat men opened fire on a procession of Moslems trying to visit a cemetery in the Croat-controlled western sector.
